change: 'the dealer is allowed to add a couple of points to that rate' is stated as a universal rule in a reach:global video, but it is false in general: the UK FCA banned discretionary (rate-linked) motor finance commission from Jan 2021 and Australia's ASIC banned flex commissions from Nov 2018. Scope it (e.g. 'In the US, many dealers can add up to a couple of points...') or describe it as something some dealers can do.

hook/loop: 'Your car discount? You quietly pay it back.' presents the markup as certain for every viewer; it only happens when the buyer finances through the dealer and the dealer marks up the rate. Soften to 'can'/'may' (e.g. 'Your car discount? You might quietly pay it back.').

turn + title: 'the loan hands it back to the dealer, one payment at a time' and the title 'How car dealers win back your discount' say the dealer recovers the discount, but the extra $1,982 interest goes to the lender and the dealer only gets a share (and the dealer reserve is usually paid to the dealer upfront, not per payment). The 'after' beat says this correctly ('the dealer keeps a share'); make the turn and title match: the buyer pays back roughly the discount in extra interest, and the dealer gets a cut of it.
promise/before (minor, fix while rewriting): the car is $35,000 with $2,000 off, yet the loan is for the full $35,000; either make the loan $33,000 or call $35,000 the amount financed.
